transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Recording link: (shared in calendar)
Shared artifacts: Optimize Studio deck (Jordan), Lagoon sample traces (Priya - partial upload), cost-model template (Jordan)

Summary:
Jordan gives a short framing: this is an Optimize Studio walkthrough focused on batching + lookahead/prefix cache (KV) recommendations and a cost model tailored to Lagoon's chat-style session workload. Maya demos the console savings simulator with a live sandbox and runs a couple of scenarios (sessionized bots, burst traffic). Customer asks about data residency, private deployment latencies, and fallback to hosted models under capacity constraints. Call ends with clear next steps: share spreadsheet, run sandbox, and follow-up with SRE deep-dive.

Topics covered:
- Workload profile: short chat sessions with bursty concurrency, average prompt length ~80 tokens, p50/p95/p99 latencies described
- Batching tradeoffs and concurrency targets
- KV/prefix caching (lookahead) economics and cache TTLs
- Quantization and model variant routing for cost vs latency
- Sandbox cost modelling with Optimize Studio
- Private vs hosted deployment considerations and audit/KMS requirements

Action items (read aloud at end)
- See metadata action_items for owners/due dates
Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining from Lagoon, really appreciate the time. I'm Jordan Park from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Maya Singh, our solutions engineer who will run the sandbox and cost sim. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Rosa: Doing well, thanks. Quick heads up we'll probably hand off to Samir for infra questions after the first 10 minutes.
[00:13] Ethan: Yeah we want to focus on cost and latency tradeoffs today, and see some concrete numbers.
[00:18] Jordan: Totally. The plan — quick framing, then Maya will demo Optimize Studio scenarios for your sessionized bot workload, and then we'll walk through a tailored cost model. We also want your traces — Priya mentioned you'd share those.
[00:28] Priya: I uploaded a sample 48-hour trace to the shared drive, it's not the full week yet but should be enough to start.
[00:33] Maya: Great, I'll pull that into the sandbox. One note — the console labels KV as "prefix cache" in some places and "K V cache" in others, so apologies if terminology flips.
[00:41] Rosa: No worries, we just need the idea.

[00:48] [Demo start — Maya sharing screen]
[00:50] Maya: Okay showing Optimize Studio home, the sandbox link Jordan shared. First tab: workload import. I selected Lagoon_sample_48h.json — shows session lengths, request arrival distribution, and concurrency heatmap. See that big spike at 10:15 last Wednesday? That's a marketing blast.
[01:07] Ethan: That's the one that almost took down our old endpoint, yes.
[01:10] Maya: Right. Next we map to a serving profile: model LLM-Redwood-16B-quant (example), sequence lengths: prompt 80, response ~120 tokens. We can toggle batching windows, max batch size, and lookahead/prefetch depth (KV lookahead).
[01:24] Priya: Walk me through lookahead — how are you measuring the benefit? I always confuse prefetch with session cache.
[01:29] Maya: Good question. Lookahead or prefetch here means we predict a subset of likely next-token KV contexts for a session and warm them in the GPU cache so subsequent calls hit hot KV. It's different from session cache which stores whole outputs. In the sim we estimate hit rate as a function of lookahead depth and session similarity, then convert hits to token-savings and lower GPU per-token compute.
[01:49] Jordan: Put another way: prefix/KV caching reduces effective model compute for repeated prefixes across sessions — it amortizes decoding cost.

[02:00] [Maya runs baseline scenario]
[02:03] Maya: Baseline no-lookahead, small batch window (10ms), p50 latency 120ms, cost per 1M tokens: $X (shows number). Now toggle batching to aggressive (50ms, max batch 32), p50 moves to 140ms but cost drops by ~22%.
[02:24] Priya: That's a noticeable cost drop, but our product team won't accept p50 >150ms on core flows. Is there a sweet spot?
[02:31] Maya: We can hit p50 ~130ms with modest batching (25ms) and lookahead depth 3 — that yields ~15% cost reduction while keeping latencies under your 140ms internal target.
[02:43] Ethan: Did you include quantized variants in the model routing?
[02:46] Maya: Yes, second tab shows multi-variant routing. For non-critical flows we route to the 8-bit quant variant (lower throughput but cheaper), and keep 16-bit for pinned low-latency paths. The console sim factors in model throughput differences.

[03:02] [Maya flips to cache economics pane]
[03:05] Maya: Here's the KV prefetch economics: cost of buffer + extra VRAM vs per-token savings. For Lagoon's similarity numbers (roughly 40% repeated prefixes across sessions), lookahead depth 4 is sweet — predicted cache hit ~28% and token-cost saving ~18% overall. TTL plays a role; too long and you hold VRAM for cold sessions.
[03:29] Priya: What's the VRAM or footprint estimate for depth 4?
[03:32] Maya: For the 16B quant model it's about 1.1 GB per 10k active prefixes; with your peak concurrent sessions ~3k, rough working set estimate is ~330MB. That's within our Dedicated node profile but we can also use hybrid routing.

[03:48] Samir (joined): Sorry I'm late, quick Q — if we do Private, do we still get the Studio optimizer and automatic routing? Latency to the control plane is a concern for us.
[03:58] Jordan: Yes, Optimize Studio runs locally in Private as an agent — the control plane can remain on your VPC or be customer-managed. For very sensitive setups we support an air-gapped option; in that case the optimization analytics run locally. The only difference you'll see is audit log shipping options.
[04:15] Samir: And KMS — keys must stay in our HSM.
[04:19] Maya: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for model keys and have RBAC controls; we'll include SOC2 and KMS docs in the follow-up.

[04:30] [Maya runs sensitivity sim across three windows]
[04:33] Maya: Scenario A: conservative batching + no lookahead. Scenario B: moderate batching + lookahead=3. Scenario C: aggressive batching + lookahead=5 + quant routing.
Scenario A cost baseline, Scenario B saves ~14%, Scenario C saves up to ~30% but p95 latency increases a bit. For Lagoon's SLO of p95 <400ms we caution about C in production.
[05:05] Rosa: That 30% is compelling but we need to understand tail behavior — what happens under the marketing blast spike?
[05:10] Maya: The sim includes a stress test — we model your spike and route overflow requests to a cheaper pooled variant or to hosted fallback; Redwood's smart router will failover to dedicated or alternate model region based on policy. That keeps availability at cost of quality occasionally.
[05:25] Priya: Could you show the concrete numbers for the spike scenario?
[05:28] Maya: Sure — in the spike sim with lookahead 3 and batching 25ms, cost per hour increased X, but p99 stayed under 1.2s; with C scenario p99 jumped to 2.4s. So we recommend B for now.

[05:45] [Jordan jumps in to explain cost model spreadsheet]
[05:48] Jordan: The spreadsheet maps tokens to GPU-seconds by variant, then adds amortized KV memory cost, and traces routing percentages. I put a conservative estimate for your concurrency shape and a more aggressive row for peak marketing blasts.
[06:03] Ethan: Can you make a row for our international region — we have EU traffic and require data residency for EU tokens. Does the model account for region egress cost?
[06:11] Jordan: There's a regional toggle — confirm we should add a separate EU model cluster and include inter-region egress. We'll add that to the spreadsheet.

[06:20] Maya: Quick aside — sometimes Optimize Studio's auto-suggest will propose a lookahead depth that overfits to the trace. We include conservative guardrails and we recommend running the sandbox for a week of real traffic or a replay of a full week's traces.
[06:36] Priya: We'll aim to export a full week's traces by EOD Friday.
[06:40] Rosa: A security question — if cached KV contains PII or sensitive prefixes, how is that encrypted at rest/in RAM?
[06:47] Maya: KV entries are stored in memory on the inference node; in Private deployments you control the node. For hosted we encrypt at rest and in transit and we can enable enclave-like protections for the hottest keys. We'll send the security appendix with details.

[07:02] [Customer asks about benchmark reproducibility]
[07:05] Samir: We like to run our own benchmarks. How reproducible are the console sims vs our internal bench runs on our hardware?
[07:11] Maya: The sim uses a model throughput profile calibrated to common GPU families; for Private we can run a validated micro-benchmark kit on your nodes to align numbers. That is included in the follow-up.

[07:26] [Discussion on rollout strategy]
[07:28] Jordan: Suggested rollout: 1) Sandbox + replay week traces (validate sims), 2) Canary with lookahead=1 and batching moderate for 2 weeks, 3) Increase lookahead to 3 and ramp batching if SLOs hold. We'll provide change templates for your infra team.
[07:44] Priya: Sounds good. One question — how do you measure regression in quality if we route to quantized variants?
[07:50] Maya: We hook into your eval harness or run a blind A/B test on a sampled subset. Optimize Studio can run rollout experiments and track quality deltas on your prompt set. If quality drops beyond thresholds, automatic fallback occurs.

[08:05] [Wrap-up — read action items]
[08:08] Jordan: Quick recap of commitments: Jordan will share the cost-model and studio link; Maya will set up the sandbox; Lagoon will share full-week traces; we'll schedule SRE deep-dive. Any other asks?
[08:18] Rosa: Please include our security contact on the doc.
[08:21] Jordan: Will do.
[08:23] Ethan: Thanks everyone, this was helpful — the numbers make it tangible.
[08:27] Priya: Thanks.
[08:30] Jordan: We'll follow up with dates. Bye.
